questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Describe Azure authentication methods
questions.question: Select the TWO statements that are correct according to this unit.

options.text: Single sign-on (SSO): a Microsoft passwordless authentication option using a device-bound credential and PIN or biometrics.
Single sign-on (SSO): signing in once and using that authenticated identity across multiple trusted applications.
Authentication: the process of establishing the identity of a user, service, or device using credentials.
Multifactor authentication (MFA): Microsoft cloud-based identity and access management service.
Authentication: something the user knows, such as a password or PIN.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Authentication — the process of establishing the identity of a user, service, or device using credentials; and Single sign-on (SSO) — signing in once and using that authenticated identity across multiple trusted applications.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Describe Azure authentication methods
questions.question: Which TWO statements accurately reflect the concepts covered in this unit?

options.text: Knowledge factor: something the user knows, such as a password or PIN.
Multifactor authentication (MFA): something the user is, such as a fingerprint or facial biometric.
Multifactor authentication (MFA): requiring an additional authentication factor so a password alone is not sufficient.
Knowledge factor: Microsoft Entra capabilities for integrating and controlling access to cloud and on-premises applications.
Knowledge factor: a hardware-based passwordless authentication option supported by Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Multifactor authentication (MFA) — requiring an additional authentication factor so a password alone is not sufficient; and Knowledge factor — something the user knows, such as a password or PIN.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Describe Azure authentication methods
questions.question: Select TWO correct statements about the material in this Microsoft Learn unit.

options.text: Possession factor: an app that can support MFA and passwordless sign-in.
Possession factor: using identity and device state with tools such as Intune and Conditional Access.
Inherence factor: Microsoft Entra capabilities for integrating and controlling access to cloud and on-premises applications.
Inherence factor: something the user is, such as a fingerprint or facial biometric.
Possession factor: something the user has, such as a phone or security key.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Possession factor — something the user has, such as a phone or security key; and Inherence factor — something the user is, such as a fingerprint or facial biometric.

questions.description: Microsoft Learn unit: Describe Azure authentication methods
questions.question: Which TWO statements are consistent with the unit content?

options.text: Windows Hello for Business: a Microsoft passwordless authentication option using a device-bound credential and PIN or biometrics.
Windows Hello for Business: Microsoft cloud-based identity and access management service.
Inherence factor: technology that synchronizes identities between on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID.
Microsoft Authenticator: technology that synchronizes identities between on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID.
Microsoft Authenticator: an app that can support MFA and passwordless sign-in.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Windows Hello for Business — a Microsoft passwordless authentication option using a device-bound credential and PIN or biometrics; and Microsoft Authenticator — an app that can support MFA and passwordless sign-in.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security

questions.question: Choose the TWO accurate statements.

options.text: Authentication: the process of establishing the identity of a user, service, or device using credentials.
FIDO2 security key: using identity and device state with tools such as Intune and Conditional Access.
FIDO2 security key: a hardware-based passwordless authentication option supported by Microsoft Entra ID.
